sections.title: Choose questions before adding variants
paragraphs: A small brand can compare one sample in each category before multiplying colors and sizes. Ask a wearer to evaluate the intended use: everyday cotton fit, low-visibility edge beneath an outfit, or high-waist coverage. Keep each trial tied to the model, size and fabric. This produces an evidence-based shortlist rather than a line sheet filled with speculative trends.

Review component minimums, sample costs, size availability and timing in the written quotation. Public catalogue references are a starting point, not a promise that a custom material or color can be made at the same terms. Update the assortment if the verified offer differs from the initial idea.

sections.title: Make the website answer the actual buyer question
paragraphs: A useful product page shows front and back images, body and gusset materials, rise, size range and an honest sample request route. A collection page can compare verified styles without manufacturing a product count or performance claim. News articles should answer one question and link back to the exact products and sourcing service.

Review search performance later in Search Console to see which terms generate impressions and clicks for this site. Broad consumer volume may be high while a manufacturer's article draws a much narrower audience. Update the pages that attract qualified sample enquiries, not merely the ones that resemble popular consumer searches.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Does a popular search term prove a product will sell? No. It identifies interest in a category, not demand for a specific model.
Should every page target cotton, seamless and high-waist together? Only when the actual product supports all three attributes.
What is the next practical step? Choose a model, obtain its current specification and request a sample against a written use case.

title: Underwear Leg Opening Elastic: A Fit Review Checklist
description: Specify leg-opening elastic for private-label underwear through placement, finished measurements and wearer feedback instead of a generic tightness claim.
coverAlt: DIYASI DYS206 cotton bikini brief showing the leg opening on a real catalogue style
imageCaption: DYS206 is a cotton bikini reference. The image cannot establish elastic tension or wearer comfort; review those on the actual sample.
intro: A leg opening that looks neat in a photograph may press, gape or shift when worn. For a private-label underwear order, define the intended coverage, finished opening and elastic application on a named sample. Compare feedback at the same size and under the same wear conditions before asking a factory to change tension. DYS206, DYS219 and DYS214 show different bikini, high-leg and boyshort shapes; they are starting references, not proof that one elastic setting works for every silhouette.

sections.title: Describe the opening before discussing comfort
paragraphs: Record the model, sample size and intended leg line. Mark the front and back points where the opening should sit, then note the finished opening measurement and how the elastic is enclosed or exposed. A high-leg brief may place the edge differently from a boyshort even when both are labelled the same size. The pattern and fabric must be reviewed together with the elastic.

Ask the maker which measurement is taken with the garment relaxed and which is taken under a stated extension. Do not substitute a supplier's unstated stretch percentage for a fit trial. If the edge digs in, note the exact area and wearer position; if it gaps, note whether the issue appears at the front, seat or both. Photos with the wearer's permission can make corrections clearer.

sections.title: Test the selected size range, not only one sample
paragraphs: Review at least the sizes that best reveal the fit risk in your proposed range. A comfortable middle size does not establish that the smallest or largest size has the right leg-opening balance. Keep the wearer profile and trial method consistent, and record each observation against the sample version. If the same issue recurs, ask whether the pattern grade, elastic cut length or material recovery needs review.

The DYS206 bikini, DYS219 high-leg brief and DYS214 boyshort have distinct leg shapes. Their catalogue descriptions do not publish leg-opening measurements or elasticity. Request the exact specifications for the chosen model and approve a physical sample rather than transferring a measurement from one shape to another.

sections.title: Close the change before bulk production
paragraphs: A revision request should identify the sample version, the location of the problem, the proposed change and the expected result. Compare the revised sample against the original under the same conditions. Check that changing the leg edge has not altered coverage, side-seam position or the appearance of a matched waistband.

Put the accepted pattern, material, elastic details and finished measurements into the production specification. Define who signs off size-set samples and how an out-of-tolerance opening will be handled. This turns subjective wear feedback into a repeatable inspection reference without pretending that a single fit claim applies to every customer.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Can a photo prove the elastic is comfortable? No. It can show placement and finish, but pressure and movement need a wearer trial on the actual size and fabric.
Should every size use the same elastic cut length? No universal rule follows from the catalogue. Agree size-specific measurements and review the grade on samples.
What should go into the approval record? Include model, sample size and version, measurement method, wearer observations, approved elastic specification and the decision owner.

title: High-Waist Underwear: Review Waistband Roll-Down
description: Use a repeatable sample review to diagnose high-waist underwear roll-down across rise, waistband, body fabric and size grading.
coverAlt: DIYASI DYS314 high-waist seamless full brief with broad waistband area
imageCaption: DYS314 is a high-waist full brief reference. A product photograph cannot show how its waistband behaves in movement.
intro: A high-waist brief may look smooth on a flat lay and still fold or slide during wear. Roll-down is an observation, not a diagnosis: waistband height, body length, fabric recovery and fit at the waist and hip can all matter. Use one named sample and a defined size when comparing changes. DIYASI's DYS314 seamless full brief, DYS219 high-leg cotton brief and DYS210 long-leg cotton brief illustrate different constructions that should not be treated as interchangeable.

sections.title: Separate the symptom from its possible causes
paragraphs: Record where the waistband sits when first put on and where it moves after sitting, bending and walking. Note whether an edge folds locally, the whole top slides downward or the body fabric bunches below it. These outcomes can lead to different pattern or component changes. A request to 'make it tighter' alone is too vague and could create new pressure points.

Measure front rise, back rise, top opening and waistband height using the method agreed with the factory. Photograph the garment flat and on the wearer only with permission. Note the wearer's waist and hip measurements and the size selected. Compare the symptom on the same wearer and under the same trial steps after each revision.
rows: Is the opening or elastic too restrictive?

sections.title: Compare construction without assuming a universal fix
paragraphs: DYS314 is described as a seamless full brief with a polyamide-spandex body and cotton gusset. DYS219 and DYS210 are cotton-spandex high-waist references with different leg shapes. Those catalogue facts can guide sample selection, but they do not establish an anti-roll performance result. Ask for the actual waistband construction and finished measurements before comparing them.

A wider waistband is not automatically more stable. The knit, edge finish, body shape and wearer proportions affect the outcome together. If a buyer changes fabric or rise, test the combination rather than assuming the previous approval transfers. Keep the approved size chart and material version attached to the trial record.

sections.title: Approve the full range and production reference
paragraphs: A size-set review should include the sizes that may reveal a change in waistband behaviour. Specify what a pass looks like for your brand, who performs the wear review and which movement steps are used. Do not claim that the product never rolls; document the conditions under which the samples were assessed.

When the revision is accepted, preserve an approved reference sample and the corresponding pattern, material and measurement sheet. Confirm any color or branding changes that could alter the waistband. Production inspection can then compare construction and dimensions with the approved reference, while fit claims remain limited to actual wearer evidence.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Does a higher rise prevent roll-down? Not by itself. The top opening, body length, material and wearer's shape also need review.
Can the factory solve the issue from a flat photograph? A photo helps locate a fold but cannot show the full movement or pressure pattern.
What should an inquiry include? Share model, size, wearer measurements, movement notes, sample version and the intended rise.

title: Bonded vs Stitched Gussets: Underwear Sample Checks
description: Compare bonded and stitched underwear gusset attachment by edge finish, placement, wash review and documented sample approval.
coverAlt: DIYASI DYS323 bonded Brazilian seamless brief with cotton gusset
imageCaption: DYS323 provides a bonded-gusset reference; DYS311 is listed with a stitched cotton gusset. Confirm the construction on the selected sample.
intro: A cotton gusset does not tell a buyer how its edges are attached. DIYASI lists DYS323 and DYS322 with bonded cotton gussets, while DYS311 specifies a stitched cotton gusset. That makes them useful references for discussing attachment, but no catalogue label proves durability or comfort. Examine the actual inside and outside of each sample, record the construction and agree what must remain intact after the buyer's specified care review.

sections.title: Identify each layer and attachment point
paragraphs: Ask for the body composition, lining composition, gusset dimensions and edge-attachment method separately. A bonded edge may involve an adhesive or film system that the finished catalogue photo cannot identify. A stitched edge may vary in seam type, stitch placement and thread. The buyer should request construction details for the chosen model rather than infer them from the word 'seamless'.

Inspect the front and rear ends of the gusset and both side edges. Note exposed edges, wrinkles, visible adhesive, skipped stitches or a shift away from the intended placement. Record the sample size and version; a narrow gusset on one size cannot define the expected coverage across a range.
rows: Edge integrity under agreed wash method

sections.title: Use a stated care method for comparisons
paragraphs: Agree a laundering and drying method based on the intended care instructions before reviewing a sample. Photograph the same edge before and after the review, and record whether a bond lifts, a seam changes or the lining distorts. One satisfactory wash is not a lifetime guarantee. The number of cycles and acceptance criteria should be part of the buyer's agreed test plan, not invented from a product description.

If a change is requested, ask for a revised sample using the intended fabric, lining and attachment method. Changing the body knit or lining can alter how the edge behaves. Reconfirm the whole assembly rather than signing off only an isolated swatch.

sections.title: Write an approval that production can follow
paragraphs: The specification should distinguish the gusset lining from the body fabric and show where each attachment begins and ends. Include images of the approved inside and outside, measurement points, approved care instructions and the responsible reviewer. If a supplier proposes another bonding material or stitch, treat that as a documented change.

For DYS323, DYS311 and DYS322, confirm the current source specification and sample details with the factory before placing an order. The catalogue records a construction starting point, not a test certificate or a promise that every batch uses the same unreviewed component.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Is a bonded gusset always less visible? Visibility depends on the full fabric and edge construction; inspect the selected garment under intended use.
Does stitched mean more durable? Neither method guarantees durability without a defined material, process and care review.
What should be retained after approval? Keep the physical sample, construction images, care method and change record together.

title: Lace Trim on Underwear: Stretch & Placement Checks
description: Review lace trim placement, stretch and sample comfort against the exact underwear body fabric before approving private-label production.
coverAlt: DIYASI LS006 lace-trim cotton Brazilian brief showing lace placement
imageCaption: LS006 combines a cotton-spandex body with polyamide-spandex lace. Verify the final trim and placement on the selected sample.
intro: Lace trim changes the shape and feel of an underwear edge, so it should be specified as a component rather than a decorative note. DIYASI's LS006 Brazilian brief, LS005-142 brief and LS005 thong list cotton-spandex bodies with polyamide-spandex lace. Their different silhouettes make placement and stretch especially important to review. A catalogue image shows the design direction; it does not prove that the trim behaves the same across sizes or colors.

sections.title: Map the trim on the actual pattern
paragraphs: Mark where lace begins and ends at the waist, side and leg opening. Record the finished width, orientation, color and the side that touches the wearer. A lace edge near the leg may need a different fit review from lace placed only at the waist. Share front, back and inside images with the factory so the intended placement is unambiguous.

Keep the lace specification separate from the body fabric and gusset. The source composition for the three referenced LS styles identifies the body and lace, but the selected order still needs confirmed component details, shade and availability. Do not use a body-fabric composition claim to describe the entire garment.
rows: Is it on the intended edge?
Does the edge cause unwanted pressure?
Body and lace under agreed light

sections.title: Check component stretch as a system
paragraphs: If lace and body fabric recover differently, the finished edge may ripple, tighten or pull out of shape. Ask the maker how it controls trim length during attachment and request the intended measurement method. Compare the finished garment, not only loose lace or fabric swatches. A fit review should identify the sample size and the wear conditions in which the issue appears.

Inspect inside seams and lace joins for rough points or uneven attachment. Record observations without claiming a medical or skin-safety outcome. If the trim is changed for color or cost, treat the substitution as a new component that may need fit and care review.

sections.title: Protect the approved look in production
paragraphs: Save an approved trim swatch or sample with a component code, color reference and attachment drawing. Specify any acceptable shade variation and who decides borderline cases. The factory and buyer should agree how to handle a lace delivery that differs from the approved reference before cutting begins.

Review the selected size range and the intended care method. A lace edge that passes one static inspection may still shift after use or washing. Document the test conditions and decision rather than claiming universal comfort or longevity from a single photograph.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Can the same lace be used on every silhouette? Placement and length need review against each pattern and size range.
Is matching color enough? No. Stretch, edge feel, width and attachment also affect the finished garment.
What should a sample request include? Name the model, lace area, color reference, component details and intended wearer review.

title: Men's No-Fly Pouch Underwear: A Sample Fit Review
description: Compare no-fly men's underwear samples using pouch shape, body and lining materials, seam position and movement feedback.
coverAlt: DIYASI M004 men's mid-rise no-fly trunk with a shaped front pouch
imageCaption: M004 is listed as a no-fly trunk. Its photo cannot confirm pouch support or the precise lining composition for an order.
intro: A no-fly front describes access construction; it does not define pouch volume or fit. DIYASI lists M004 as a mid-rise no-fly trunk, while M007 is a boxer brief and M001 a low-rise brief. These give buyers different starting shapes for a men's underwear range. The catalogue describes polyester-and-spandex bodies with modal in the pouch or gusset area, but precise percentages for these men's models still need confirmation. Keep body, lining and waistband details separate in the sample brief.

sections.title: Specify the front construction and intended wearer
paragraphs: Identify whether the selected model has a functional fly, a decorative front seam or a closed front. Request inside and outside sample photographs and a construction drawing where the difference matters. State the intended rise, leg length and size range. A buyer cannot judge pouch shape from the product title alone, and a no-fly label should not be presented as a support claim.

Ask for finished front-rise and relevant pouch measurements with clearly defined measurement points. Fit comments should say whether the issue is at the seam, center front, under the pouch or waistband. Avoid substituting one wearer's preference for an objective performance result; record the wearer profile and conditions of each trial.

sections.title: Evaluate the lining as a separate component
paragraphs: A modal pouch or gusset does not make the entire garment modal. For M004, M007 and M001, the source descriptions distinguish body and pouch materials but do not provide every component percentage. Request the order-specific composition and finish before writing a retail material claim. If a printed or alternative version is selected, confirm that its specification is the same rather than assuming the model name proves it.

Look for seam bulk and placement where the pouch joins the body. Ask how a changed lining or stitch would affect the approved sample, then review the revision in the finished garment. Do not infer breathability, support or reduced friction from the fiber name alone.

sections.title: Turn fit notes into an approved reference
paragraphs: Keep a versioned record of sample measurements, inside details and wearer comments. If a revision addresses pressure at one seam, check that it has not altered the waistband position or leg fit. Review representative sizes to see whether grading preserves the intended shape.

Before bulk production, approve a named physical sample and a written specification for front construction, component materials, seams, size chart and labeling. The factory can then compare later production against an actual reference rather than a phrase such as 'comfortable pouch'.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Does no-fly mean the front is seamless? No. A closed front can still use shaping seams; inspect the selected model.
Is a modal pouch a modal garment? Not unless the full garment composition supports that wording.
Can one size establish the fit? It is a useful starting point, but the planned size range needs a grading review.

title: Printed Underwear: Approve Artwork & Strike-Offs
description: Plan a printed underwear strike-off review around artwork scale, placement, color and the exact fabric before approving bulk production.
coverAlt: DIYASI M004 Print men's boxer brief showing a printed body fabric
imageCaption: M004 Print is a catalogue print reference. Confirm the final artwork, print method and approved fabric with the factory.
intro: A print that looks clear on a digital artwork file may change when it wraps around a curved underwear pattern. A strike-off, or a physical print sample made for review, helps buyers check scale, placement and color on the intended material. DIYASI lists printed men's M004, M006 and M007 variants, but their catalogue photographs are not approval records for a new brand's artwork. Keep the print specification tied to the exact model, fabric and production version.

sections.title: Build a print brief that can be measured
paragraphs: Supply an editable artwork file with repeat size, orientation and color references. Mark any motif that must align at the center front, side seam or back panel. State whether a placement is essential or whether normal cutting variation is acceptable. A phrase such as 'same as the picture' does not tell the factory how to place a new graphic across pattern pieces.

Identify the base fabric and intended colorway. A print proof on another fabric can mislead the buyer about shade, stretch and hand feel. Ask the supplier to confirm the print method and any applicable component minimums in writing. Do not quote a production tolerance until it has been agreed for the actual artwork and cutting plan.

sections.title: Inspect the physical strike-off and sewn sample
paragraphs: Review the printed fabric first, then a garment made from it. Check whether a motif is distorted across the waistband, pouch and leg opening. Look at both relaxed and gently stretched states, using a consistent method. If a design crosses a seam, check the permitted mismatch on the finished sample rather than expecting an impossible perfect match by assumption.

Compare the print after the care review specified for the product. Record color movement, cracking or loss of detail if observed; do not advertise a test result without a documented method and outcome. If the pattern or fabric changes, a previous strike-off may no longer be a valid reference.

sections.title: Release the correct version to production
paragraphs: Label the approved artwork, strike-off and garment sample with the same revision code. Specify which file controls colors and which physical sample controls appearance. Agree who approves a bulk shade or placement deviation, and request a production sample if a component changes before cutting.

M004 Print, M006 Print and M007 Print are three distinct catalogue models. Confirm the exact source page and current material description for the selected variant. The printed and plain versions should never be merged in a quote or line sheet merely because their model numbers look similar.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Is a digital mock-up enough? It communicates design intent, but a physical sample is needed to assess print on the selected fabric and pattern.
Can one strike-off cover all colorways? Each colorway needs the agreed approval evidence, especially if its base fabric or ink combination changes.
What should be attached to the order? Include the approved artwork revision, fabric, color references, placement plan and signed sample record.

title: Underwear Bulk Shade Bands: Control Color Variation
description: Use approved shade references and component-by-component checks to manage color variation in bulk underwear production.
coverAlt: DIYASI LS005-142 cotton brief with contrast between body fabric and lace trim
imageCaption: LS005-142 is a body-and-lace reference. Its catalogue image is not a bulk shade-band approval.
intro: A lab dip can approve a color direction, but bulk fabric, lace, elastic and printed panels may still arrive in visibly different shades. A shade band is a physical range of bulk material samples reviewed against an agreed standard. For underwear with multiple components, define whether the goal is a close match or an intentional contrast. LS005-142 includes body and lace; DYS223 is a cotton brief; M006 Print adds printed material. They illustrate why one color name is not a complete production control.

sections.title: Set the standard and viewing conditions
paragraphs: Identify the approved color reference and the material it applies to. Record whether the body, lace, waistband, thread and labels must match or may differ. Agree the viewing light and background used for comparison. A phone image can help communicate an issue, but camera settings and screens make it unreliable as the sole shade standard.

Ask the factory to show a representative range from the bulk material, not only the best-looking swatch. Keep the approved shade band or clear numbered physical samples with the order file. State who makes the accept, rework or reject decision when a delivery sits at the edge of the agreed range.
rows: Does each lot fit the shade band?
Is the match or contrast intentional?
Does bulk retain the approved appearance?

sections.title: Review lots before mixing them in garments
paragraphs: A style may use several fabric rolls or trim deliveries. Ask how lots are identified and whether pieces from different lots will be mixed in the same garment or carton. Compare components side by side before cutting, then inspect a finished sample because seam placement and lighting can change the visible effect.

If a material substitute is proposed, do not assume its shade will match the approved item. Check composition, finish and appearance again. Color consistency should be evaluated along with the approved construction and size; a visually matching but different material is not automatically an acceptable replacement.

sections.title: Close the decision in the production record
paragraphs: Record the accepted range, the rejected examples, the sample date and the person who approved them. State what happens if a later lot falls outside the range. For a multi-color order, keep each colorway's references separate so a factory does not apply one approval to another style or season.

The public DIYASI catalogue does not establish a universal shade tolerance. Ask for a production plan and material evidence for the selected model and quantity. A written color decision is more useful than a claim that all units are 'perfectly identical'.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Does a lab dip approve bulk goods? It approves a target or sample; bulk material still needs comparison under the agreed process.
Can body and lace use one color code? They may need separate references because components and finishes can render a shade differently.
What belongs in a shade-band record? Include material and lot IDs, viewing conditions, physical references, decision and approver.

title: Underwear Barcode & Variant Labels: Proof Before Print
description: Check style, size, color and pack-level barcode artwork against an approved SKU matrix before printing private-label underwear packaging.
coverAlt: DIYASI DYS223 cotton brief used as a single-style reference for size and color variants
imageCaption: DYS223 is a product example; its catalogue photograph does not show an approved retail barcode or packaging label.
intro: A correct garment can still become unsellable when its printed size, color or barcode identifies another variant. Before printing underwear packaging, join the product specification to a controlled SKU matrix and ask the brand's barcode owner to verify the assigned identifiers. DIYASI's DYS223, LS006 and M001 illustrate different product families; their catalogue model numbers are not retail barcodes. The buyer must supply or approve the retail identifiers and market-specific wording for the intended sales channel.

sections.title: Create one source of truth for every sellable variant
paragraphs: List style, model, color, size, pack quantity and intended market in a table. Assign the correct brand SKU and barcode value to each sellable combination. Make it explicit whether a multipack has its own identifier and how it differs from each garment inside. Do not copy a barcode from a sample pack onto another color or size.

Keep barcode ownership with the party responsible for the retail listing. The factory can print supplied artwork but should not be asked to invent an identifier. If a marketplace or retailer has its own label rules, obtain the current specification from that channel and reconcile it with the brand's packaging plan.

sections.title: Review the physical proof, not only the file
paragraphs: Print a proof at the intended size and on the proposed label or card material. Check readable text, sufficient quiet space around the code under the printer's specification, and the position after the package is assembled. Scan the proof with the equipment or workflow used by the receiving channel, then verify that the decoded value maps to the intended SKU. A successful scan alone does not prove the associated product data is correct.

Check packaging artwork alongside the garment and care label. The fiber and care claims need order-specific evidence and market review; a generic template should not be reused blindly. If a size scale changes after fit approval, update the variant matrix and every related label file before printing.

sections.title: Control revisions through packing
paragraphs: Give each artwork file and matrix a version number. The production order should identify the approved version, quantity and packing unit. At the first packing run, inspect a finished unit from every relevant variant and compare it with the matrix. Keep the signed proofs and record any correction before bulk labels are applied.

Ask the factory to identify leftover labels from earlier versions and how they will be segregated. This is a practical way to prevent a corrected artwork file from being undermined by old printed stock. Confirm the final barcode and label responsibilities in the written quotation.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Is a factory model number a retail barcode? No. It identifies a catalogue style; the retail identifier belongs to the brand's sellable-unit system.
Does a scanner pass approve all labels? No. Text, product mapping, size and pack quantity also need review.
When should proofs be repeated? Repeat them after any change to the SKU matrix, artwork, packaging format or receiving-channel requirement.

title: Underwear Carton Protection: A Shipment Checklist
description: Define carton contents, moisture protection and receiving checks for underwear shipments with a packing plan suited to the actual order.
coverAlt: DIYASI DYS202 cotton bikini brief shown as a product reference for shipment planning
imageCaption: DYS202 is a garment reference. Confirm the actual folded presentation, bag and carton plan for the order.
intro: Underwear is lightweight, but its presentation can still be damaged by poor packing, moisture or a carton that is difficult to reconcile at receipt. A shipment plan should connect the finished garment, inner pack and outer carton to the SKU matrix and destination requirements. DIYASI's DYS202 cotton bikini, LS006 lace brief and M005 men's boxer illustrate different material and shape considerations. Their product pages do not promise a single carton specification for every buyer.

sections.title: Define the pack around the actual product
paragraphs: Decide whether garments are folded individually, grouped by size or color, or packed as a retail multipack. Record the approved fold, insert, bag, label and carton quantity. Lace edges and printed surfaces may need different contact or folding review from a plain cotton brief. The right choice depends on the sample presentation and shipping route, not a stock photograph.

Specify carton dimensions and weight only after the packed sample and quantity are agreed. Ask the factory how it prevents crushed presentation, shifted bundles and mixed variants. Avoid claiming that a particular bag or desiccant always solves moisture risk; material choice and destination rules must be checked for the actual shipment.

sections.title: Make carton marks match the packing list
paragraphs: Give each carton an identifier and define which style, color, size and quantity it contains. A mixed carton needs a clear breakdown. Reconcile the count of individual garments, retail packs and outer cartons; these are not always the same unit. Keep the commercial invoice and packing list aligned with the actual goods and buyer requirements.

Photograph a representative packed carton and the label before shipment. A scan or visual check at dispatch can catch a swapped variant, but the receiving party should still compare the arriving cartons with the documents and inspect for visible damage.

sections.title: Agree what happens after a transport problem
paragraphs: The buyer and supplier should decide how damage will be recorded at receipt, including carton photos, lot or carton IDs, affected quantities and the time window for notification under their contract. This article does not set transport liability; those terms depend on the agreed sale and carrier arrangements.

For a new pack format, test a representative shipment configuration using a method appropriate to the route and risk. Record the conditions and results if a test is performed. Do not market a pack as transit-tested solely because a sample arrived intact once.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Can one carton count be used for all styles? Different garment sizes, folds and packaging can change the safe and practical count.
Should every carton be mixed? Mixed and single-variant cartons serve different fulfillment plans; decide from the receiving workflow.
What should be signed off? Approve the packed sample, carton matrix, marks, document totals and damage-reporting process.

title: Underwear Line Sheets: A Wholesale Buyer Checklist
description: Build a private-label underwear line sheet with verified styles, materials, sizes, images and order questions that help retailers compare a real collection.
coverAlt: DIYASI DYS201 low-rise cotton bikini brief as a line-sheet style reference
imageCaption: DYS201 is one catalogue style. Check its current specification before placing price, availability or performance claims in a buyer line sheet.
intro: A line sheet should help a wholesale buyer identify the exact underwear styles available for discussion, not imply that every catalogue photograph is a stocked variant. Start with verified model references, silhouettes, material components and the sizes and colors the factory can confirm. DIYASI's DYS201 cotton bikini, DYS323 bonded seamless brief and M007 men's boxer brief can illustrate different product families. Their images and source specifications are useful starting evidence, while prices, current stock and production timing require order-specific confirmation.

sections.title: Give each style a clear identity
paragraphs: Use one row or panel per model and show the model number, product name, front and back imagery, silhouette, rise and relevant construction. Where the image shows a sample color, label it as an example until the order colors are confirmed. Do not merge a printed and plain men's variant under one stock-keeping unit merely because their names are similar.

Link to the live product page or keep the source reference in the working file so a buyer can ask about the actual style. Describe components precisely: for example, DYS323 lists a polyamide-spandex body and cotton gusset; the modal reference on M007 relates to the pouch or gusset, not automatically to the entire garment.

sections.title: Separate public facts from commercial terms
paragraphs: A catalogue MOQ can be a starting reference, but custom colors, labels, fabric and packaging may change component minimums. Put a date and scope on every quote. If the line sheet is used for several markets, identify which size scale and labeling plan applies to each. The buyer should be able to tell whether a figure is confirmed for a particular order or only a discussion point.

Do not publish a made-up wholesale price or a universal lead time to fill a blank cell. A useful line sheet can instead say 'quote on request' and ask for quantity, color breakdown, branding and destination. This keeps buyer expectations aligned with the factory's actual production review.

sections.title: Turn the sheet into a sampling decision
paragraphs: Arrange styles by use case or construction so the buyer can compare a coherent group: cotton everyday basics, bonded seamless styles or men's options. Add a short sample decision for each, such as checking leg opening, gusset attachment or pouch fit. Link those questions to the product page and the selected sample rather than generic quality language.

Version the sheet whenever a model, image or commercial term changes. Before sending it externally, have the product owner verify current source details and the sales team check the offer terms. Track which models attract questions, then improve the relevant product and service pages with confirmed answers.

sections.title: Common buyer questions
paragraphs: Does the line sheet prove inventory is available? No. Availability needs a current factory confirmation for the selected variant.
Can a sample photo stand for every color? Only if clearly labeled as a sample image and not presented as all available options.
What makes the sheet actionable? Exact model references, clear unknowns and a route to request samples or a scoped quotation.

title: How to Choose an Underwear Manufacturer: Buyer Checklist
description: Evaluate an underwear manufacturer by product fit, sample evidence, production responsibilities and order controls before choosing a private-label supplier.
coverAlt: DIYASI factory workspace with rows of sewing stations and hanging garments
imageCaption: An existing photograph of the DIYASI production workspace. Confirm the people, processes and production arrangements relevant to your own underwear order.
intro: Choose an underwear manufacturer by checking whether its materials, construction experience and order controls fit the product you want to develop. Start with identifiable samples, then confirm who handles pattern work, production, inspection and communication. A factory photograph or a low quotation cannot answer all those questions. DIYASI's cotton DYS201, bonded DYS323 and men's M007 illustrate three different sample briefs that can help a buyer assess a supplier against a concrete requirement.

sections.title: Write the product requirement before comparing suppliers
paragraphs: Define the intended customer, silhouette, material direction, size range and branding changes. Use front, back and inside references for the selected garment. A supplier experienced in one construction may need a different development process for another, so compare its response to the actual brief rather than its total catalogue size.

For example, DYS201 is a cotton-spandex bikini, DYS323 uses a polyamide-spandex body and bonded cotton gusset, and M007 is a men's boxer brief with modal lining. A useful supplier discussion identifies the relevant pattern, material and attachment questions for each, without treating them as interchangeable basics.
rows: Can the supplier develop this garment?
Named roles and any subcontracted operations
Who controls each stage of the order?
Measurement reports and an agreed inspection plan
Written quotation, component minimums and milestones
Versioned feedback and a named order contact
Can changes be traced and closed?

sections.title: Verify the business and production arrangement
paragraphs: Confirm the contracting business name, factory location and the roles of the people handling the enquiry. Ask which operations happen at the proposed site and which are performed elsewhere. Subcontracting should be discussed clearly so the buyer understands who approves materials, monitors work and resolves defects.

When a capability or certificate matters to the order, request current evidence with the relevant entity, site, scope and validity. A logo displayed on a website is not enough to establish that a particular product, material or shipment falls within that scope. Check discrepancies before relying on the claim.

sections.title: Use samples to assess the working relationship
paragraphs: Send the same documented brief to shortlisted suppliers and record what each sample represents. Compare measurements, inside finish, material identity and the response to specific corrections. A sample that looks attractive but arrives without its version or material reference is difficult to reproduce reliably.

Review how the supplier handles uncertainty. A clear request for missing dimensions or clarification of a logo is useful evidence of the process. Keep unanswered questions visible, particularly those affecting fit, component minimums or the final production specification.

sections.title: Compare the complete proposal before committing
paragraphs: Separate garment cost, development, labels, packaging, inspection and shipping terms. Record when material and sample approvals are required and what happens if changes are requested. A shorter stated lead time may assume stock materials or earlier approvals that another quotation does not include.

Create a decision record showing evidence, open questions and the person responsible for resolving each one. Discuss an initial order only after the sample direction and commercial scope are clear. Factory selection is a sequence of verified decisions rather than a score based on one attractive feature.

sections.title: Manufacturer-selection questions
paragraphs: Is a factory always preferable to a trading company? Compare the actual responsibilities, transparency and ability to deliver your specification. The business label alone does not settle those questions.
Does a good sample guarantee the bulk order? No. The approved sample becomes a reference for production controls and inspection; it does not replace them.
What should I send DIYASI first? Share the chosen model numbers, target market, quantities and requested changes, plus any construction or documentation requirements that affect your decision.

reading.label: Explore the factory and quality overview

title: Thong vs G-String vs T-String: An Underwear Buyer Guide
description: Compare thong, G-string and T-string references by back width, side construction and rise. Prepare a precise private-label sample request with DIYASI models.
coverAlt: Mint green DIYASI DYS230 T-string with a narrow front panel and slim side straps
imageCaption: DYS230 is the catalogue's low-rise T-string reference. Request the back view and finished measurements when comparing it with DYS204 and DYS224.
intro: Thong, G-string and T-string names describe related minimal-coverage styles, but suppliers do not use the terms with identical definitions. Compare the actual back panel, side construction, front coverage and rise before choosing a private-label reference. DIYASI lists DYS224 as a thong, DYS204 as a G-string and DYS230 as a low-rise T-string. Their model numbers and physical samples provide a more precise buying language than the silhouette names alone.

sections.title: Compare the visible construction, not a rigid naming rule
paragraphs: In common usage a G-string often has a narrower string-like back than a thong, while T-string can refer to the arrangement of narrow straps. These are useful starting descriptions rather than a universal measurement standard. In particular, the DYS230 description refers to a minimal Y-shaped back despite the T-string product name.

All three selected catalogue styles list 95% combed cotton and 5% spandex. That shared material direction does not establish matching fabric weight, strap tension or fit. Ask for the inside and back views alongside the front image before deciding which style matches the intended collection.
rows: Width and shape of the back panel
Slim sides, front coverage and actual back outline

sections.title: Put coverage and strap dimensions into the brief
paragraphs: Use a labelled front-and-back drawing to identify side width, back width at an agreed point, front rise and gusset dimensions. If the design includes straps, define where their width and length are measured and whether the measurement is taken relaxed or under an agreed condition.

Show how the narrow back meets the gusset and waistband. A request to make the back smaller can mean reducing panel width, changing its length or altering the attachment angle. Those changes can affect fit differently and should not be left to interpretation.

sections.title: Check pressure and stability on the sample
paragraphs: Assess the waist, side straps and joins while standing, sitting and moving. Record the position of any pressure or shifting, then discuss whether the pattern, elastic tension or construction needs revision. Simply ordering a larger size may change coverage without resolving the original issue.

Review the inside finish where components meet. Check for bulky joins, rough thread ends and uneven attachment. A minimal silhouette gives the buyer fewer visible panels to compare, making these small construction details especially useful in the sample feedback.

sections.title: Choose sizes and branding for the exact reference
paragraphs: DYS224 is listed from S to 2XL; DYS204 and DYS230 list S to XL. Confirm the range and availability for the planned order. A matching size letter does not imply the same finished measurements across the three shapes.

Identify where branding and required information can fit without crowding narrow straps or creating an uncomfortable join. Agree the label method and placement on the actual garment before approving artwork. Keep the selected model and any pattern revision together in the technical pack.

sections.title: Questions about minimal-coverage styles
paragraphs: Are all G-strings lower rise than thongs? No. Rise and back coverage are independent features; compare their measurements separately.
Does a narrower back guarantee invisible lines? No. Edge finish, size, fabric and the outer clothing also matter. Assess the finished sample under its intended clothing.
Can a front photo confirm the exact shape? It cannot show the back or inside construction. Include those views and a sample reference in the enquiry.

reading.label: Compare tanga, bikini and thong coverage
Specify measuring points in a technical pack

title: Underwear Fabric GSM: Weight, Thickness & Opacity
description: Understand what fabric GSM can and cannot tell underwear buyers. Compare weight, thickness, opacity and stretch using identified samples and material records.
coverAlt: Rear view of a black DIYASI DYS323 Brazilian brief with smooth laser-cut leg edges
imageCaption: DYS323 has a listed polyamide-spandex body. Its photograph and fibre composition do not establish fabric GSM, thickness or opacity under every wearing condition.
intro: GSM means grams per square metre: the mass of a defined area of fabric. It helps describe material weight, but it is not a direct measurement of thickness, opacity, softness or finished-garment quality. For underwear sourcing, record GSM alongside fibre composition, construction, finish and sample observations. The public specifications for DIYASI's DYS323, DYS201 and LS006 do not state GSM, so buyers should request the actual material data instead of estimating it from photographs.

sections.title: Keep weight, thickness and opacity as separate requirements
paragraphs: Two fabrics with similar GSM can have different thicknesses because their yarns, structures and finishes differ. Colour, fabric openness and stretching can also change how much light passes through a garment. A heavier specification alone is therefore an incomplete way to request more coverage.

For a useful comparison, label swatches with the fabric reference, composition, colour and finishing state. Ask whether the quoted weight is for the finished material that will be used in production, and agree how variation will be measured and assessed.
rows: Material record and agreed measurement method
Distance through the fabric under defined conditions
Measurement with stated method and pressure
How much underlying colour or detail is visible
Physical review under controlled lighting and stretch
Defined test conditions and recorded results

sections.title: Compare the same component and finishing state
paragraphs: DYS201 lists a 95% cotton and 5% spandex body. DYS323 lists an 80% polyamide and 20% spandex body with a cotton gusset. LS006 combines a cotton-spandex body with polyamide-spandex lace. Request information for the specific component being compared, rather than a single unexplained weight for the whole garment.

Garment weight includes its pattern area, trims and multiple components, so weighing a finished brief does not directly give the body's GSM. If the supplier measures a fabric specimen, record its area, preparation and method. Use a qualified laboratory when the purchasing requirement calls for standardised verification.

sections.title: Build an opacity review around intended use
paragraphs: Compare physical samples against the same background and lighting at the intended fit or an agreed extension. Include relevant light and dark colourways; a result from one colour is not automatically representative of the range. Record whether the concern is body transparency, a visible lining boundary or the garment showing through outer clothing.

These are different observations. A garment can be opaque while its seam is visible under trousers, and a smooth edge can still belong to a translucent body fabric. Describe the requirement precisely so the factory can consider material and construction changes separately.

sections.title: Approve the material before treating GSM as a buying rule
paragraphs: Choose a physical reference that meets the intended balance of coverage, handle and fit, then document its material specification. If the fabric changes, review the affected pattern and finishing details instead of assuming the previous sample approval still applies.

Include the agreed weight requirement and tolerance in the material record, with the relevant test method where needed. Do not set a universal minimum GSM for all cotton, lace and polyamide underwear: each construction has different requirements and needs its own evidence.

sections.title: Fabric-weight questions
paragraphs: Does higher GSM mean better underwear? Not by itself. The required coverage, fit, feel and durability determine whether a material is suitable.
Can GSM prove breathability? No. Mass per area does not measure airflow or moisture performance. Define and verify those requirements separately.
Can I request the same blend at another weight? Discuss it as a material change with the supplier. Availability, minimum quantities, pattern behaviour and sample work may all change.

title: Tanga vs Bikini vs Thong: Specify Underwear Coverage
description: Compare tanga, bikini and thong coverage with real DIYASI styles. Use back views, side width and finished measurements to avoid ambiguous sourcing requests.
coverAlt: Pale neutral DIYASI DYS208 cotton tanga with a striped waistband detail
imageCaption: DYS208 is DIYASI's everyday cotton tanga reference. Confirm its back shape on the linked gallery and physical sample before choosing a coverage direction.
intro: Tanga is a variable retail term, so an underwear sourcing brief should pair it with front-and-back references and measurements. In the DIYASI catalogue, DYS208 provides a cotton tanga direction between a classic brief and a minimal thong in visual coverage. Compare it with DYS202 bikini and DYS229 thong by the actual back panel and side construction. Do not assume every supplier uses tanga to mean the same amount of coverage.

sections.title: Use one identifiable style for each comparison
paragraphs: The selected DYS208, DYS202 and DYS229 styles all list 95% combed cotton and 5% spandex, with sizes S through XL. They nevertheless have different shapes and waistband details. The shared blend is a material reference, not proof of identical stretch, weight or fit.

Request back views taken at a comparable angle and identify the photographed size. Front images can make different silhouettes look similar. A side or back view is more useful for explaining the coverage change a buyer wants to make.
rows: Rear shape relative to the bikini and thong

sections.title: Describe the rear shape without inventing a coverage percentage
paragraphs: Draw the intended back outline and mark the points that should be wider or narrower. Record width at defined locations, back rise and the relationship to the gusset. A phrase such as half coverage has no reliable production meaning unless the drawing and measurement method explain it.

Keep leg-opening height separate from rear width. Raising the leg line can change the appearance from the front without producing the desired back shape. When comparing samples, note which panel edge is moving and where it should sit on the intended wearer.

sections.title: Check stability as well as the first impression
paragraphs: A fitting review should observe the back panel after sitting and walking, not just in a static pose. Record shifting, pulling or pressure at specific points. Ask the pattern team to consider coverage, opening tension and gusset placement together before changing the entire size.

Use the same body-size reference when comparing the three silhouettes. If each sample is assessed on a different fit basis, the buyer may attribute a sizing difference to the style name. Keep body measurements and finished-garment measurements in separate records.

sections.title: Give the tanga a distinct assortment role
paragraphs: A tanga may be worth sampling when customers ask for less rear coverage than a selected bikini but do not want the selected thong. Treat that as a customer requirement to validate. It does not establish that every tanga will fit the same role or sell better than another silhouette.

For the approved style, use consistent naming, diagrams and photographs across the product page, packaging and supplier documents. Explain the actual coverage in customer-facing copy. If a target market uses tanga differently, clear images and a fit description can prevent the name from carrying the whole explanation.

sections.title: Tanga buying questions
paragraphs: Is tanga always another name for thong? No. Usage varies by supplier and market. Confirm the actual pattern rather than relying on translation alone.
Is tanga the same as Brazilian? The terms can overlap in some catalogues, but they are not universal equivalents. Use the exact model and rear outline in the brief.
Can I develop a new back shape from DYS208? Ask for a pattern review with annotated changes. Confirm sampling work, material requirements and quantities before treating it as an available variant.

title: Heat-Transfer vs Sewn Underwear Labels: Buyer Guide
description: Compare heat-transfer, printed and woven labels for underwear. Review fabric compatibility, placement, legibility and sample durability before approval.
coverAlt: Dark grey DIYASI M001 men's brief with a plain black waistband and shaped front panel
imageCaption: M001 is described as a tagless design in the catalogue. Confirm the actual information-marking method on the inside sample; the front photograph does not show it.
intro: Choose an underwear label method by the information it must carry, the available placement area and its compatibility with the garment. Heat-transfer marking avoids a separate sewn label at that location; printed or woven sewn labels introduce a physical component and attachment. Neither method is automatically more comfortable or durable. Use the actual fabric, artwork and sample to review the result, and keep branding choices separate from the information required in the target market.

sections.title: Separate the brand mark from product information
paragraphs: List the logo, size, material information, care instructions and any other required details before choosing the method. They may not all belong in the same location or use the same execution. Confirm the target-market requirements before reducing text to fit a small decorative mark.

M001 provides a tagless catalogue reference, DYS223 a cotton brief for custom branding discussion, and DYS322 a polyamide-spandex thong. Their different shapes and materials are useful starting points for reviewing placement. None establishes that every proposed label process is already approved for that model.
rows: Does the process suit the body fabric and stretch?
Legibility, adhesion, appearance and handle after agreed care
Which substrate, edge finish and attachment are intended?
Text clarity, seam bulk and contact with skin
Can the weave reproduce the artwork at the chosen size?
Fine-detail readability, stiffness and edge treatment

sections.title: Approve placement on the actual garment
paragraphs: Provide a drawing with the label dimensions and distance from an identifiable seam or edge. State whether the measurement refers to the printed area or the full label component. Review the inside placement as worn so the information does not accidentally face the wrong direction.

For narrow-back or low-rise styles, available space may be limited. Check that the mark does not interfere with a bond, gusset edge or seam allowance. A placement that works on a men's brief should not simply be copied to a thong without a new sample review.

sections.title: Test the artwork and material combination
paragraphs: For a transfer, ask the supplier to select application conditions suited to the fabric and marking system. Review possible changes to colour, surface appearance or stretch, along with cracking, peeling and readability after the agreed care procedure. Do not prescribe a generic heat setting for every material.

For a sewn label, examine the edges, fold and attachment seam. Assess the garment during the fit review and after washing. Record whether an issue comes from the label itself, its location or the seam, because each calls for a different correction.

sections.title: Control artwork versions and component quantities
paragraphs: Keep a separate approved file for each size, language or information variant. Check spelling and material wording against the final garment specification, then request a proof at actual size. A readable enlarged PDF can still produce illegible text when reduced to the finished mark.

Confirm setup costs, label or transfer minimums and how unused components are handled. If materials change after the first order, review the information and process compatibility before reusing existing labels. The earlier logo approval does not automatically approve a new composition statement.

sections.title: Underwear-label questions
paragraphs: Does tagless mean no product information is needed? No. It describes an execution choice, not an exemption from information requirements.
Is a heat transfer always softer? The result depends on the marking system, coverage, material and application. Compare physical samples at the intended location.
Can the same artwork be used on cotton and polyamide? The visual artwork may be shared, but process suitability and durability need confirmation for each material and finish.

reading.label: Prepare market-specific size and label information

title: Underwear AQL Inspection: Define Defects & Sampling
description: Prepare an underwear inspection plan with a defined lot, defect categories, sampling method and release decision. Understand what an AQL result can establish.
coverAlt: Taupe DIYASI DYS215 women's cotton boxer with a wide waistband and finished leg hems
imageCaption: DYS215 provides a waistband-and-hem construction reference for an inspection brief. This catalogue image does not show a completed inspection or its result.
intro: An underwear AQL inspection needs an agreed sampling system, a defined production lot, defect categories and clear acceptance rules. AQL, or Acceptance Quality Limit, is a parameter used in a sampling system; it is not a statement that every garment was checked or that a shipment contains no more than a guaranteed percentage of defects. Prepare the inspection plan before the order is ready to ship, using the approved garment and technical specification as references.

sections.title: Define the lot and the inspection method
paragraphs: Identify the purchase order, models, colours, sizes, quantities and production status covered by the inspection. Agree how the sample will be selected across the defined lot and how variants will be represented. A few convenient garments chosen from one open carton may not represent the shipment.

ASQ describes ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 as an acceptance sampling system for inspection by attributes, with switching rules for a continuing stream of lots. If a standard is specified, agree the applicable edition, inspection level, plan and relevant rules with the inspector. Writing only AQL on a purchase order leaves important decisions unresolved.
rows: Models, variants, quantities and production status
Standard, level, plan and selection procedure
Severity definitions and agreed acceptance criteria
Connects findings to the approved specification
Decision owner, corrections and reinspection rules

sections.title: Agree defect examples for the actual underwear
paragraphs: Create an illustrated defect list with the buyer, supplier and inspector. Safety hazards, functional failures and appearance issues need distinct handling. For example, a sharp foreign object, an open structural seam and a minor cosmetic thread issue raise different concerns; their classification and response must be agreed rather than inferred from this article.

Use relevant construction references. DYS215 calls attention to the wide waistband and leg hems; DYS322 includes a bonded gusset; M007 has a men's pouch and leg construction. Check the approved requirements for those details instead of applying an unrelated garment checklist unchanged.

sections.title: Separate workmanship, measurement and test evidence
paragraphs: Record observed defects with photographs, locations and sample identifiers. Keep the counting rule explicit: a count of nonconforming garments is different from a count of individual nonconformities, because one garment can have several issues. The report should follow the agreed sampling system consistently.

Dimensional checks need the approved measuring method and tolerance. Fibre composition, colourfastness and other performance claims may require separate evidence or tests; a visual inspection does not establish them. Note which checks were performed, which documents were reviewed and which requirements remain unverified.

sections.title: Resolve findings before the release decision
paragraphs: The report should identify the lot, selected units, findings and conclusion under the agreed plan. If the lot is not accepted, record the containment or rework action and the verification needed afterwards. Do not quietly replace the inspected pieces and treat the original report as a new approval.

Keep the shipment-release decision separate from the inspector's observations where your purchasing process requires it. An accepted sample supports a lot decision within the plan's limits; it does not replace ongoing process control or establish zero defects throughout production.

sections.title: AQL questions from underwear buyers
paragraphs: What AQL should every underwear order use? There is no universal value supplied here. Agree the product requirements, defect severity and sampling plan with qualified inspection support.
Does AQL mean the same thing as inspecting a fixed percentage? No. Sample size and acceptance rules depend on the selected system and its inputs.
Is this DIYASI's inspection result? No. It is a planning guide. An actual result must identify the order, lot, date and inspection evidence.

reading.label: Choose a supplier using relevant evidence

references.label: ASQ: ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 and Z1.9 sampling systems

title: Shipping Underwear Samples: Documents & Invoice Checklist
description: Prepare underwear sample shipments with clear goods descriptions, material details, values and consignee information. Align the invoice, parcel and sample list.
coverAlt: White DIYASI M007 men's boxer brief showing the front pouch, waistband and short legs
imageCaption: Identify a sample by its actual model and garment description. M007's public listing names body and lining fibres but does not supply their exact percentages.
intro: For an international underwear sample shipment, prepare a clear goods description, quantities, material information, accurate customs value and complete recipient details. Make the invoice, shipping label and enclosed sample list consistent. Calling a parcel samples does not explain what is inside or automatically remove customs requirements. Confirm the documents and import treatment for the destination with the carrier or customs adviser before dispatch, particularly when the parcel contains several different styles or materials.

sections.title: Describe the garments beyond the word samples
paragraphs: FedEx's customs-document guidance recommends descriptions that identify what the goods are, how many there are, what they are made from and their intended use. Use the model number as an additional reference, not as a substitute for a plain description that a carrier or customs officer can understand.

A cotton women's brief such as DYS223 and a men's boxer brief such as M007 should remain distinguishable on the goods list. DYS323 includes a polyamide-spandex body and cotton gusset. Confirm the actual sample's construction and composition before using that information in shipping documents.
rows: Garment type, material, quantity and sample purpose
The actual contents of the parcel
Accurate declared value using the applicable basis
Name, address, contact and required importer information

sections.title: Resolve missing material information before booking
paragraphs: The catalogue lists M007's body as polyester and spandex and its lining as modal, without exact percentages. Do not fill the gap with a guessed blend. Request the details needed for the actual shipment and retain them with the sample record.

Tariff classification can depend on construction, garment type, fibre content and destination rules. This guide does not assign one code to every underwear sample. Ask the carrier or customs adviser to confirm the appropriate classification and any additional information required.

sections.title: Keep free samples and customs valuation separate
paragraphs: A supplier may charge for a sample or provide it without a sales charge, but that commercial arrangement does not by itself establish a zero customs value. Declare the goods accurately using the valuation basis applicable to the shipment. Avoid replacing a required description or value with a vague phrase such as gift.

Confirm who pays freight, duties, taxes and any clearance charges, and whether the consignee needs to act as importer. Do this before the package is collected so a sample needed for a fitting is not held while the parties resolve responsibility.

sections.title: Make arrival useful for the development review
paragraphs: Attach an identifier to each sample without obscuring the area being evaluated. Include a list of model, size, colour, version and the purpose of the sample, such as fit review or final-material approval. A parcel containing several unlabelled garments creates avoidable uncertainty after delivery.

Share the tracking reference and keep the document set with the order record. On arrival, reconcile the contents with the list and record any damage or missing items before starting the fit review. Carrier transit estimates and customs processing should remain separate from the factory's sample-preparation time.

sections.title: Sample-shipping questions
paragraphs: Are underwear samples always duty-free? No automatic exemption is assumed here. Treatment depends on the destination, goods and applicable procedure.
Can one parcel contain several models? It can be planned that way, subject to carrier and destination requirements. Describe the different goods accurately and reconcile the quantities.
Does DIYASI's sample timing include transit? Confirm this in the quotation. Preparation, dispatch, transport and customs are separate stages unless explicitly included.

reading.label: Keep sample versions in a technical pack

references.label: FedEx: Customs documents and accurate goods descriptions

title: Recycled Polyester Underwear: Verify Claims & Documents
description: Check recycled-polyester underwear claims by component, percentage and traceability. Review material records and claim requirements before approving labels.
coverAlt: Dark grey DIYASI M005 men's boxer brief with a black waistband and stretch body fabric
imageCaption: M005's source describes a recycled-polyester option. The photograph does not prove recycled content, a percentage or certification for a particular order.
intro: A recycled-polyester underwear claim should identify the relevant component, the substantiated recycled proportion and the records that connect the material to the order. A recycled option in a catalogue is not confirmation that every sample or shipment uses it. DIYASI's M005 source mentions such an option, while the final composition and documentation require order-specific confirmation. Keep the material claim separate from claims about recyclability, biodegradability or overall environmental benefit.

sections.title: Identify what the proposed percentage describes
paragraphs: Write down whether a percentage refers to the body fabric, the polyester component within that fabric or the whole garment by mass. These are different statements. Underwear can include a separate lining, elastic, thread and labels, so a body-fabric claim should not silently become a whole-product claim.

M005, M004 and M007 are catalogue examples with polyester-spandex bodies and modal lining. Their public material descriptions do not establish exact component percentages or recycled content for a chosen order. Request the final bill of materials and evidence for the specific material being proposed.
rows: Composition and recycled-content records with a clear basis
Does the evidence cover this supply?
Whether wording or logo use is permitted

sections.title: Connect certification evidence to the material supply
paragraphs: Textile Exchange describes the RCS and GRS as standards for third-party certification of recycled materials and chain of custody. Review the relevant entity, site, activities, material scope and supporting supply records. A certificate copied from a different business or material cannot establish the claim for your garment.

Ask what transaction or traceability documentation is required under the applicable programme and which records will accompany the order. Textile Exchange also publishes a standards transition programme, so confirm the version and timeline relevant to the supply rather than relying on an old logo or summary.

sections.title: Approve claim wording before printing packaging
paragraphs: For the US market, the FTC's Green Guides summary cautions against broad, unqualified claims such as green or eco-friendly and explains that partly recycled products or packaging need qualified recycled-content claims. Use specific, supported language and review the requirements in every destination market where the claim will appear.

Certification does not automatically substantiate every environmental statement a brand might make. Confirm the rules for the exact wording and any proposed logo. A recycled-content record does not itself prove that the finished underwear can be recycled through a customer's local collection system.

sections.title: Keep material approval and product performance connected
paragraphs: If an approved body fabric is replaced with a recycled-content option, review the resulting material, fit, colour and care requirements on the actual sample. Do not assume equivalent appearance or performance solely because both materials are described as polyester-spandex.

Retain the approved claim text with the material reference and order documents. On reorders, check whether the material source or specification changed and whether the supporting records still cover the new supply. Update product copy and labels when the substantiated claim changes.

sections.title: Recycled-material questions
paragraphs: Is M005 automatically certified recycled underwear? No such blanket claim is made here. Confirm the selected material and relevant documentation for the actual order.
Does recycled polyester mean biodegradable? No. Recycled origin and biodegradability are different properties and need different evidence.
Can I use an RCS or GRS logo because a supplier mentions the standard? Only after confirming that the product and claim meet the applicable requirements. A catalogue mention is insufficient.

reading.label: Review body fabric and pouch composition

references.label: Textile Exchange: Recycled Claim Standard and Global Recycled Standard

title: Underwear Multipacks: Plan Styles, Colours & Quantities
description: Plan an underwear multipack by garment mix, size consistency and component quantities. Check colour balance, packaging and replenishment before quoting.
coverAlt: Rear view of a mint green DIYASI DYS229 cotton thong with a finished waistband
imageCaption: DYS229 is an individual catalogue style, not a ready-made multipack offer. Pack composition, colours, packaging and quantities need project-specific confirmation.
intro: An underwear multipack is a defined combination of garments sold as one unit. Decide whether it contains one repeated silhouette, several colours or different shapes before requesting a quote. Then calculate the required garment quantities for each component and check size consistency across the set. DIYASI's DYS229 thong, DYS202 bikini and DYS214 boyshort can support that planning conversation, but they do not constitute a pre-approved pack or a fixed multipack price.

sections.title: Choose a pack with one clear customer purpose
paragraphs: A repeated-style pack may serve a customer who already knows the fit, while a mixed-shape set may help a brand introduce different coverage choices. Validate that purpose with customer evidence before adding complexity. More garments in a pack do not automatically make the offer more attractive.

The three example styles list cotton-spandex compositions, but their patterns differ. DYS229 is a thong, DYS202 a bikini and DYS214 a boyshort. If combining shapes, explain the coverage of each and review whether the same labelled size provides the intended fit across the set.
rows: Consistent fit, shade and unit presentation
Each colour approved and available in the required quantity
Fit and size-label consistency across different patterns
Packaging appropriate to the intended sales channel
Packed dimensions, component costs and artwork

sections.title: Calculate the component quantities before discussing minimums
paragraphs: For an illustrative three-colour pack with one garment in each colour, 100 packs require 300 garments: 100 of each colour. If the pack instead contains two black garments and one accent colour, the same 100 packs require 200 black and 100 accent garments. These are planning examples, not DIYASI minimum-order offers.

Repeat the calculation for every pack size and style combination. Then confirm garment, colour, trim and packaging minimums separately with the supplier. A catalogue minimum per style does not automatically define the minimum for a custom printed box or every colour in the pack.

sections.title: Approve the fit and packed presentation together
paragraphs: For a mixed-shape set, review a complete pack in the relevant size references. Keep each garment's measurement specification separate while checking that the intended customer can use the set consistently. Do not correct a fit mismatch by simply changing the size sticker on one component.

Request a packed sample after the garment combination is settled. Check folding, orientation, visible size and colour information, and whether the contents match what the package promises. Confirm packaging dimensions using the actual garments rather than an empty mock-up alone.

sections.title: Plan reorders at both pack and component level
paragraphs: A pack can become unavailable when one required component runs short even though the other garments remain in stock. Track the quantities needed to assemble a complete set and discuss how colour or style substitutions will be handled. A substitution changes the offer and needs explicit approval.

Give the sellable pack its own identifier and retain a list of the exact component variants and quantities. Keep the order allocation and carton packing instructions aligned with that list. This creates a clear handover from assortment planning to production and warehouse receiving.

sections.title: Multipack planning questions
paragraphs: Does DIYASI already sell these three models as a fixed pack? This article proposes a planning approach. Confirm the desired configuration, feasibility, quantities and price for the actual project.
Is a multipack always cheaper per garment? Not necessarily. Packing work, materials, artwork and component quantities affect the final quotation.
Can different sizes be mixed in one pack? Specify the intended use and component sizes clearly. Do not leave the factory or receiving warehouse to infer the assortment.

reading.label: Map pack SKUs to carton quantities

title: Underwear Product Photography: A Brand's Shot List
description: Prepare an underwear product-photo brief with front, back, inside and detail views. Match images to approved styles and keep fit, colour and branding accurate.
coverAlt: White DIYASI LS006 cotton brief with floral lace at the waistband and leg openings
imageCaption: The LS006 front image shows the lace-and-cotton design. A complete product story also needs back, inside and detail views of the approved garment.
intro: An underwear product-photo brief should show the garment's shape, back coverage, inside construction and important details using the approved sample. Connect every image to a model, size, colour and version so product pages describe the item a buyer will receive. Front-only photography is often insufficient for underwear because the back and lining distinguish many styles. Plan the evidence shots first, then add styling images for the brand's presentation.

sections.title: Start with a product-specific shot list
paragraphs: LS006 needs views that explain its lace waistband, leg trim and Brazilian back. DYS302 needs a clear view of its thong shape and stitched gusset. M004 benefits from a view of the men's trunk silhouette, waistband and inside pouch. The best detail list follows the garment rather than a fixed number of decorative images.

Decide which photographs will support the product listing, wholesale line sheet and sample discussion. A styled hero can introduce the collection, while consistent front and back views let buyers compare models more easily. Keep the two uses clear in the brief.
